analysis:
On 1 August 2012, Ashok Gehlot said Rajasthan was the first state to introduce a Right to Hearing Act. He said the Act would provide a time-bound hearing on complaints related to governance.

The Rajasthan Right to Hearing Act, 2012 received the Governor's assent on 21 May 2012 and was implemented on 1 August 2012. It provides for a public hearing officer, first and second appellate authorities, and penalties of Rs 500 to Rs 5,000.

Deccan Herald and The Times of India reported that Rajasthan was the first state to implement such a law. The statement held.
